findings.finding: The root-cause premise that every one of the 143 tests executes POSIX shell is not borne out for the 4 shellcheck-lint tests. `test_pinned_shellcheck_lints_all_provider_shell_bodies_without_skips` and the 3 `test_provider_shell_bodies_pass_pinned_shellcheck[...]` cases only run the `shellcheck` binary on a file written with `Path.write_text`. On Windows, `write_text` writes CRLF line endings, which most likely makes shellcheck fail with SC1017 (a text-encoding/newline defect, not a missing-shell one). A `/bin/sh` capability skip would hide a test that can be fixed and run on Windows (write with `newline="\n"`).

findings.location: Approach — posix_shell_available / requires_posix_shell definition; Context — routes 1–3
scenarios: A host with /bin/sh but no working `bash` (e.g. a minimal container) does not skip, and the route-1 tests fail.
A future Windows image whose drive root contains bin\sh makes the probe True even though shebang execution is still impossible.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to the Approach: '/bin/sh presence is used as a proxy for a POSIX host (bash on PATH and kernel shebang execution); hosts with /bin/sh but no bash are out of scope.' Alternatively, also require `shutil.which('bash')` to resolve to a non-WSL path for route-1 tests.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State and justify that /bin/sh executability is used as a proxy for the `bash`-on-PATH and shebang-execution routes, or name in the reason string the single capability actually probed, so the mark doesn't claim capabilities it never checks.
evidence: Plan: "reason=\"needs a POSIX shell at /bin/sh and shebang-script execution; this host has neither\"" (one os.access check backs a two-capability claim)
Plan route 1: "`bash ...` / `bash -c` ... On the runner `bash` is the WSL launcher"
tests/infra/test_mcp_entrypoint.py:15-17 explains the precedent covers only the literal /bin/sh: "Every shell launch below uses the literal /bin/sh ... A PATH lookup would mislead"
findings.finding: The plan uses one probe, an executable `/bin/sh`, to stand in for all three failure routes it lists: `bash` on PATH, direct execution of shebang stubs (`#!/bin/sh` or `#!/usr/bin/env python3`), and the literal `/bin/sh`. The skip reason claims 'this host has neither'. The precedent it cites only covered tests that call the literal /bin/sh. The plan does not show that /bin/sh present ⇔ `bash` resolvable ⇔ the OS can run shebang scripts. Those tests would only be skipped correctly where all three come and go together.
findings.location: Approach — `requires_posix_shell` definition and reason string; Context — routes 1–3
scenarios: A Windows host with Git for Windows or MSYS: `bash` resolves on PATH and works, /bin/sh is absent. The route-1 tests are skipped even though they could run, which hides real coverage; this is acceptable but should be stated.
A host where /bin/sh exists but `bash` does not (minimal Alpine/BusyBox images). The mark does not skip, and route-1 `bash -c` tests fail with FileNotFoundError and the reason string is misleading.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Run `gh workflow run test.yml --ref <branch>` before merging, and state the back-out: re-add the failing node ids to the deselect file.
evidence: "Windows: `gh workflow run test.yml --ref main` after merge"
findings.finding: Windows validation happens only after merge to main (`gh workflow run test.yml --ref main`). There is no pre-merge Windows run on the branch and no back-out step if that run fails. By then the deselect lines are already removed on main.
findings.location: Testing — Windows bullet
scenarios: A marked test still fails on Windows, for example a fixture that shells out before the skip is evaluated, or a missed parametrize case. The advisory job turns red on main, and no restore step is defined.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the Testing bullet to dispatch the sweep on the feature branch before merge, keep the post-merge run on main for the AC, and add 'If any un-deselected test fails, restore its line in the .args file in a follow-up commit.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either model the posix-shell skip on the existing CapabilityProbe + registered-marker + conftest `pytest_runtest_setup`/`record_counted_skip` pattern, or state in the plan why a plain skipif is preferred for this capability.
evidence: tests/_sandbox_capabilities.py:32-37 defines `CapabilityProbe` 'Result of an operation-based capability probe'; process_table_probe, semgrep_settings_file_probe and posix_named_semaphore_probe all return it
tests/conftest.py:245-262 registers marker `requires_posix_named_semaphore` and skips in pytest_runtest_setup via `record_counted_skip(item.config, reason)`
Plan: '`posix_shell_available(sh: str = "/bin/sh") -> bool` ... `requires_posix_shell = pytest.mark.skipif(not posix_shell_available(), ...)`'
findings.finding: The plan adds a second, parallel capability-skip style to tests/_sandbox_capabilities.py: a bare `bool` probe plus a module-level `pytest.mark.skipif` object. The same module and its conftest already use a different pattern for capability skips. Probes return the `CapabilityProbe(available, reason)` dataclass. A named marker (`requires_posix_named_semaphore`) is registered in conftest.py. A `pytest_runtest_setup` hook skips through `record_counted_skip`, so skips show up in the 'sandbox compatibility skips' summary, including xdist aggregation.
findings.location: Approach, first bullet (posix_shell_available / requires_posix_shell definition); tests/_sandbox_capabilities.py
scenarios: A later reader finds two capability-skip idioms in one helper module and cannot tell which one new capabilities should follow.
The ~164 Windows skips do not appear in the counted 'sandbox compatibility skips' terminal summary, while semaphore skips on the same run do.

findings.finding: Two tickets edit the same shared files, with no dependency edge or ownership statement. This plan removes 21 lines from path-separators.args, which is owned by bug arctic-unsecular-esok. It also makes deletion of posix-shell.args and its test.yml `@` line conditional on arctic-unsecular-esok's landing order. The plan does not say whether arctic-unsecular-esok must drop those 21 tests from its own scope.
findings.location: Context — 21 path-separators tests; Approach — 'whichever lands second deletes it'
scenarios: arctic-unsecular-esok also tries to fix or un-deselect the same 21 tests, so the work is duplicated or the edits conflict.
Each ticket assumes the other will delete posix-shell.args, so an empty file and its test.yml line are left behind.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'At merge, if posix-shell.args has no non-comment lines, delete it and remove `@.github/windows-sweep-deselect/posix-shell.args` from test.yml.' Post a note on arctic-unsecular-esok transferring the 21 tests to this ticket.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that parametrized subsets use `pytest.param(..., marks=requires_posix_shell)`. Add an AC that the number of Windows tests skipped with the capability reason equals exactly the number of removed deselect lines.
evidence: "`tests/unit/workflow/test_bridge_provider_wrappers.py` (5 `four_environment_matrix` cases, ...)"
"or as module `pytestmark` where every test in the module runs a shell (`tests/scripts/test_feature_branch_e2e_scenario4.py`, ... `tests/scripts/test_cast_gerrit_verified_vote.py`)"
findings.finding: The plan does not say how to mark the subset of parametrized cases that need a shell, nor guard against over-skipping. It says to apply `@requires_posix_shell` 'to each affected test function' and module `pytestmark` where 'every test in the module runs a shell'. But test_bridge_provider_wrappers.py has only 5 `four_environment_matrix` cases deselected. Decorating the whole function, or a whole module such as test_cast_gerrit_verified_vote.py, would also skip on Windows cases that currently pass, and no AC detects that coverage loss.
findings.location: Approach — 'Apply `@requires_posix_shell` to each affected test function, or as module `pytestmark`'
scenarios: A whole parametrized function is decorated, so non-shell params that passed on Windows are now SKIPPED.
A module-level pytestmark covers tests that were never deselected, so Windows coverage shrinks silently.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Approach: 'Where only some parametrize cases run a shell, attach the mark per case via pytest.param(..., marks=requires_posix_shell); use module pytestmark only where the module's collected test count equals its deselected-line count.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a bash capability check (e.g. `shutil.which("bash")`, or a `requires_bash` mark) for the route-1 tests, or apply it alongside `requires_posix_shell`, so tests that invoke `bash` skip where bash is absent.

"`requires_posix_shell = pytest.mark.skipif(not posix_shell_available(), reason="needs a POSIX shell at /bin/sh ...")`"
Platform fact: FreeBSD ships `/bin/sh` but installs bash only via ports/pkg, at `/usr/local/bin/bash`.
findings.finding: The probe keys on `/bin/sh`, but route-1 tests run `bash ...` / `bash -c`, and the `four_environment_matrix` cases symlink `bash`. On a POSIX host with `/bin/sh` but no bash, the mark does not skip and those tests fail. Examples are FreeBSD (no bash in base) and minimal Alpine containers. The capability checked is not the capability the tests use.
findings.location: Approach — `posix_shell_available(sh: str = "/bin/sh")` / `requires_posix_shell`
scenarios: BSD developer workstation/server: `/bin/sh` exists, so `requires_posix_shell` does not skip. The bash-invoking tests then error with `FileNotFoundError: 'bash'` instead of skipping with the capability reason.
